cosy-lesson.title: "Maybe if we underpaid politicians and overpaid teachers, there would be smarter people and less stupid laws.": Anonymous (often attributed to Morgan Freeman)

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Prejudice – preconceived opinion that is not based on reason or actual experience.

p.em: Example: Overcoming deep-seated social prejudice requires education and exposure.

cosy-blockquote.p: Governance – the action or manner of governing a state, organization, or society.

p.em: Example: Good governance requires absolute transparency, accountability, and fairness.

cosy-blockquote.p: Inequality – difference in size, degree, circumstances, or social status.

p.em: Example: The new laws aim to address the growing economic inequality in the country.

cosy-blockquote.p: Democracy – a system of government by the whole population; popular representation.

p.em: Example: A free and independent press is a fundamental pillar of any democracy.

cosy-blockquote.p: Propaganda – biased or misleading information used to promote a political cause.

p.em: Example: The state media was used to spread political propaganda during the crisis.

cosy-blockquote.p: Tyranny – cruel, unreasonable, or arbitrary use of power or control.

p.em: Example: The citizens fought courageously to liberate their country from tyranny.

cosy-blockquote.p: Reform – make changes in something in order to improve it.

p.em: Example: The education system is in desperate need of comprehensive structural reform.

cosy-blockquote.p: Solidarity – unity or agreement of feeling or action, especially among individuals.

p.em: Example: The strike was supported by a massive show of public solidarity.

cosy-blockquote.p: Justice – just behavior or treatment; the quality of being fair and reasonable.

p.em: Example: The victims of the disaster are still waiting for basic legal justice.

cosy-blockquote.p: Corruption – dishonest or fraudulent conduct by those in power.

p.em: Example: The investigation uncovered deep-seated corruption in the local government.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
How does the pursuit of prejudice influence our perception of success and failure in modern life?
★ When was the last time you had to confront prejudice in your own personal journey?

Is it possible to find true balance when governance is either completely absent or excessive?
★ How comfortable are you with allowing governance to guide your daily decisions?

Why do we often struggle to cultivate inequality even when we know it is beneficial?
★ Have you ever felt a deep sense of conflict regarding inequality in a relationship?

How does democracy reshape our emotional landscape during times of intense change?
★ Can you share a moment from your childhood where democracy felt completely natural?

Can propaganda act as a silent shield against the demands of social conformity?
★ How do you personally nurture propaganda when you feel emotionally exhausted?

How do our childhood experiences shape our relationship with tyranny as adults?
★ Have you ever had to choose between social conformity and personal tyranny?

In what ways does reform challenge the rigid boundaries of logical thinking?
★ Who in your life best embodies the essence of reform, and what have they taught you?

How does embracing solidarity change the way we handle interpersonal conflict?
★ In what area of your life do you feel solidarity is most desperately needed right now?

Is justice a quality of quiet solitude, or does it thrive in noisy communities?
★ How has your personal understanding of justice shifted over the last five years?

What is the most profound lesson that corruption can teach us about our own nature?
★ If you had to describe your personal experience with corruption in one word, what would it be?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: collaborative task or visual analysis in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: A comparative reflection on our habits and self-perceptions.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: 1-on-1 guided visual description and task response with teacher.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Look at the prompt and discuss your response with your teacher:

cosy-blockquote.p: A comparative reflection on our habits and self-perceptions.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
In the future, technology will enable us to digitize and share our experience of prejudice directly. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How would you personally adapt if prejudice became entirely obsolete in tomorrow's world?

The rapid speed of modern society will eventually make governance an obsolete concept. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you be willing to use technology to artificially boost your capacity for governance?

Future educational systems will prioritize the cultivation of inequality over traditional academic skills. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How do you want future generations of your family to remember your relationship with inequality?

As artificial intelligence advances, machines will exhibit a superior capacity for democracy compared to humans. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If you could design a futuristic school, how would you teach the value of democracy to children?

In the coming decades, propaganda will become a highly commercialized luxury commodity. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you fear a future where propaganda is fully managed or monitored by digital algorithms?

The survival of human civilization will depend on our collective ability to practice tyranny. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How do you personally prepare for a future where tyranny is increasingly rare?

Future generations will look back at our current understanding of reform with deep skepticism. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If you could send a single message about reform to people living 100 years in the future, what would it be?

Global digital connectivity will make true solidarity incredibly difficult to maintain in the future. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you choose to live in a futuristic utopia that completely guarantees solidarity at the cost of your freedom?

In the future, social status will be determined by a person's capacity for justice rather than wealth. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ What role do you hope justice will play in your own personal future over the next decade?

A world fully governed by logic will have no space left for the mystery of corruption. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If a machine could perfectly replicate your experience of corruption, would you still value it?

ul.li: Incorrect: He have went to Paris → Correct: He has gone to Paris ((Present perfect third-person singular 'has' + past participle 'gone'.))

Incorrect: We discussed about the problem → Correct: We discussed the problem / had a discussion about the problem (('Discuss' is transitive and takes no preposition, or use 'have a discussion about'.))
Incorrect: I am agree with you → Correct: I agree with you ((Use 'agree' directly as a verb rather than using it with the auxiliary 'am'.))
